[issue by no-name-provided]
### Bug Description

Mod author here. A modpack with only the latest dev version of [NNP Fluidlogging](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/nnp-fluidlogging) and sodium-neoforge-0.8.12+mc1.21.1 running on neo 21.1.235 has some odd behavior. Specifically, logged blocks always render as though they contained water and the F3 screen fails to display the correct fluid.

I noticed no issue with fluid interactions, retrieving the correct fluid, or fluids flowing out of logged blocks.

I noticed no interesting errors in the log (just some access level clash notifications), so I'm guessing you're inadvertently bypassing one of my mixins. Do you have a custom fluid tesselator?

### Reproduction Steps

Load up a minimal pack, place a slab, and dump a bucket of lava in it. Creative mode fine.

### Log File

[latestlog.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29732250/latestlog.txt)

### Crash Report

[crashlog.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29732519/crashlog.txt)

[comment by jellysquid3 (member)]
Yes, Sodium completely replaces the fluid renderer, and the block renderer for that matter. If you have mixins to any of Minecraft's code, it will not work with Sodium, and there is no way to avoid that.

If you are using the Fabric Rendering APIs, you can intercept block rendering and emit geometry as you'd like from your block models -- which is fully supported when using Sodium.

For the fluid renderer, this is more difficult (since the game hardcodes about everything), but Fabric still has an interface to hook fluid rendering (see [`FluidRenderHandler`](https://maven.fabricmc.net/docs/fabric-api-0.154.0+26.1.2/net/fabricmc/fabric/api/client/render/fluid/v1/FluidRenderHandler.html)) and allows you to emit geometry however you'd like. Please note however that it means you are responsible for providing the entire fluid renderer (maybe you can dispatch it to the modified-vanilla renderer if you _really_ want) and that has performance implications since you won't be using any of Sodium's code for it.

[comment by no-name-provided (none)]
Why do you think I might be using fabric APIs? Not to be snippy, I just thought it was very clear I was building against Neoforge?

Can we just suppress your redirects? I honestly don't care _that_ much about supporting any one performance mod, and you make this sound like a "proper" fix would be a large project. I suspect all I need to do is replace instances of level#getBlockState#getFluidState with level#getFluidState. My other mixins will then query my neo chunk attachment. I really don't care about the rest of the rendering pipeline - I want to make as few changes as possible to whatever would happen if my mod weren't installed.

Edit: to put it another way: I'm not doing custom rendering, I'm just telling the game to render a different fluid.

[comment by jellysquid3 (member)]
Well, it is still possible to use the Fabric APIs on NeoForge, which is typically what we recommend to people instead of trying to mixin to our mod. If you don't want to do that, then options are limited since NeoForge doesn't provide a standard way of hooking this.

If you are extending the chunk data and need to access that data at mesh times, it will require modifications to [`LevelSlice`](https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/blob/dev/common/src/main/java/net/caffeinemc/mods/sodium/client/world/LevelSlice.java#L48). That class is responsible for copying all "relevant" world state for a given area into a buffer that can be used safely by other threads. It also implements the relevant interface (`BlockAndTintGetter`) that is then passed to every render function for querying block states, fluid states, etc.

How exactly you go about this is up to you, since with Mixins you are far outside any prescribed API.

[comment by no-name-provided (none)]
Thanks for following up. To be clear: your mod isn't compatible with NeoForge [chunk attachments](https://docs.neoforged.net/docs/1.21.1/datastorage/attachments)? That must break a lot of things. Do you support the AuxiliaryLightManager (another Neo utility that adds data to levels/chunks)?

Ah, yeah, I see a (and hopefully, though probably not, "the") problem: 
```
@Override
    public @NonNull FluidState getFluidState(BlockPos pos) {
        return this.getBlockState(pos)
                .getFluidState();
    }
```
needs to be
```
@Override
    public @NonNull FluidState getFluidState(BlockPos pos) {
        return this.
                .getFluidState(pos);
    }
```

[comment by jellysquid3 (member)]
Chunk attachments are not a rendering feature, and NeoForge itself does not copy them into `RenderSectionRegion` for use in off-thread meshing. If you are accessing chunk data attachments from the meshing code, it probably means you are accessing the global world object, which is not thread-safe regardless of the presence of Sodium.

[comment by no-name-provided (none)]
Ah, yes, RenderChunkRegion. Normally, I do indeed use `(chunk.wrapped.getData(FLUID_STATES).getOrDefault(pos, chunk.getBlockState(pos).getFluidState()));` to get my attachment holder, and I did have to fiddle with things a bit to avoid crashes on worldgen (mostly deferring lighting checks to AuxiliaryLightManager).

It's not an issue in vanilla Neo, at least not on 1.21.1. In newer versions of Minecraft, there were rare threading errors, but they seemed to stop when I changed my attachment to a ConcurrentHashMap (as opposed to a regular HashMap).

I'll try using the same mixin on your code that I used in vanilla and see if everything breaks. If it does, I might have to write this compatibility off. Thanks for the info!

[comment by no-name-provided (none)]
Building against your mod was surprisingly difficult (jar in jar not being recognized by IntelliJ and your mod not loading into my dev instance). Once I got it figured out, the fix seemed deceptively simple: replacing two calls to `getFluidState()` with calls to `getFluidState(pos)` and wrapping your `LevelSlice#getFluidState` with

```
    @WrapMethod(method = "getFluidState(Lnet/minecraft/core/BlockPos;)Lnet/minecraft/world/level/material/FluidState;")
    private FluidState getFluidState(BlockPos pos, Operation<FluidState> original) {
        ChunkPos chunkPos = new ChunkPos(pos);
        if (level.hasChunk(chunkPos.x, chunkPos.z)) {
            
            return level.getFluidState(pos);
        } else {
            
            return original.call(pos);
        }
    }
```

Interestingly, the check for loadedness is necessary; the log errors (and solution) make it seem like you're rendering chunks on the client that you aren't first retrieving from the server (which breaks Neo chunk attachment syncing). I'm sure there's fiddliness somewhere (Neo's AuxiliaryLightManager has trouble updating, and fluids probably don't display properly in those unloaded chunks), but I think this may be good enough for a first pass.

Again, thanks for the information. It would make sense to make a FAQ for Neo devs listing the things you break (and recommended workarounds). And how to set up the dev environment.

[comment by jellysquid3 (member)]
Setting up a developer workspace and using Sodium's API is described here: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/wiki/CaffeineMC-Maven-&-Config-API

Sodium cannot access chunk data that the server has not received yet, and it requires all neighbors to be received before it begins rendering, so there is likely a problem somewhere else in your code.

[comment by no-name-provided (none)]
I've seen that page. I assumed it was outdated, for Fabric, or a WIP. It really didn't have the information I needed. I meant something more like:
- The difference between [artifact] and [artifact-mod] is "..."; you probably want to use...
- To reference Sodium at compile time, you must manually add the jar-in-jar dependencies (Forgified Fabric API)
- To use Sodium in your dev environment at runtime, you must add a copy of the mod jar to "run/mods"
- etc.

It's unlikely the problem is in my code, since this only happens when your mod is installed and it's resolved by adding a check to a mixin to your code (a check that isn't required elsewhere). Your `LevelSlice#getFluidState` attempts to query blocks in chunks that aren't known to the client (the precise neo log message is `[net.neoforged.neoforge.network.handlers.ClientPayloadHandler/]: Received synced attachments from unknown chunk` - IIRC: that happens when the client isn't currently tracking the chunk the attachment is associated with).

[comment by douira (contributor)]
That warning message is referring to the fact that the client has received a packet containing an attachment for a chunk that doesn't exist on the client. See https://github.com/neoforged/NeoForge/blob/26.2.x/src/client/java/net/neoforged/neoforge/client/network/ClientPayloadHandler.java#L203 I don't see how this could possibly be related to sodium, which sits on top of the client's chunk store, and not between it and the server, or on the server.

[comment by no-name-provided (none)]
I believe that, more generally, it applies to any chunk the client isn't actively tracking (chunks that aren't [fully] loaded on the client). I could be misremembering, but doesn't your mod increase render distance and create a distinction between rendering a chunk and loading it (for ticking and such)? I assumed that was the issue - that you were rendering chunks (that I then needed to query) without actually asking the server to send you updates. My impression is that this isn't a problem in vanilla because chunks are generally fully loaded if they're in render distance.

[comment by douira (contributor)]
You must be thinking of a different mod, we don't do any of those things.
